guide.account.body:
Settings > Account lets you change your password or log out. If you forget the password, the login page has a link to start over.
Starting over erases all data for good and needs the setup code from the file setup-code.txt in the app's data folder. Afterwards the app begins again from the welcome screens. Make a backup first if you may want your data back.
guide.account.title: Account, password and erasing everything
guide.activities.body:
In Settings > Activities you add, rename and archive your habits. Each belongs to one area, has a weight from 1 (a small step) to 3 (a big one) and the days of the week it applies to: a habit set only for Monday and Thursday shows up in the questionnaire only on those days.
Keep the list short: a few habits per area that you can really keep. Add a short description if a habit needs a reminder of what counts: it shows under the name in the questionnaire. A habit can also aim for a number of times in the week instead of fixed days: skipping early in the week is free, and it only counts against a day once the goal can no longer be reached. Archiving never deletes history. An archived habit can also be deleted: it then leaves your lists, while past reports keep it. Reports that can still be edited (today and yesterday) follow your changes when you open them; older days stay as they were.
guide.activities.title: Your activities and weights
guide.backups.body:
Everything is saved in one data folder, and the app makes a backup every day at the time you choose (Settings > Account > Backups). If the device was off at that time, the backup is made as soon as it is on again.
In Settings > Account > Backups you can also download an export of your data (CSV, JSON and your journal as text) to read it or take it elsewhere; it is not a backup.
You can also back up and download a file at any moment, and restore from a saved backup or from a file. Before a restore, the app backs up the current state first.
guide.backups.title: Backups and restore
guide.basics.body:
Personal OS is a mirror, not a judge. Each evening you note which of your habits you really kept, and over time you see the shape of your days across six areas: Physical, Discipline, Social, Intellect, Career and Mindset.
It measures behaviors, never results. There are no streaks, ranks or points to chase, and nothing is ever sent to anyone.
guide.basics.title: What it is for
guide.calendar.body:
The calendar in the dock is for remembering, not judging. Pick a day, add an event with a title, an optional time, a category and notes, and choose if it repeats (daily, weekly, monthly or yearly).
Changes apply to every repeat of an event. The calendar never creates points.
guide.calendar.title: Calendar
guide.data.body:
Your data lives only on your device, in one folder. There are no accounts to pay for, no hidden costs and no tracking.
Personal OS is open source under the AGPL-3.0: the code is on GitHub, where you can report problems and suggest ideas.
guide.data.title: Your data, cost and license
guide.evening.body:
Open Questionnaire in the dock and tick what you did today. You can also write a free line about the day. When you finish, the day is recorded.
Yesterday can still be corrected until the next evening; older days are read-only. If you skip a day, it simply stays empty.
If you want, you can choose a time before which today's report cannot be filled in (Settings > Activities), so you tick things at the end of the day.
guide.evening.title: The evening questionnaire
guide.home.body:
Home shows the trend of each area (week or month, all six or three at a time) and a six-month heatmap of the days you filled in.
The Star compares the six areas together over the last 7 or 30 days. Every evening is kept exactly as it was: open More > Review and tap a day to read it.
guide.home.title: Home, Star and looking back
guide.lede: How Personal OS works, in a few minutes.
guide.mascot.body: In Settings > Account > Mascot you can add a photo, choose the name the app uses for you, write a short note and, if you like, your birth year. Only you see them, and they are saved with the rest of your data.
guide.mascot.title: Mascot (your profile)
guide.phone.body:
You can keep the app on your phone like any other app. On an iPhone, open it in Safari, tap Share and choose Add to Home Screen. On Android, open it in Chrome and choose Install app (or Add to Home screen) from the menu.
It opens full screen, with its own icon. Your data stays on your own server: the phone only shows it.
A phone reaches the app only if it can reach your server, for example through Tailscale. Browsers allow installing only over https or on the same device, so on a private network use an https address (Tailscale can provide one).
guide.phone.title: On your phone
guide.plugins.body:
Extra features are plugins. In Settings > Plugins you can switch them on or off: a mood tracker in the evening questionnaire, a journal for longer writing, a daily quote under the date on Home, and more to come.
In Settings > Appearance > Dock you choose which pages sit in the dock and in what order, up to seven in all; the rest stay in More.
Each plugin lists the permissions it asks for before you turn it on. Turning a plugin off never deletes its data.
guide.plugins.title: Plugins
guide.review.body:
The review (in More, or in the dock if you add it in Settings > Appearance > Dock) looks back at a week, a month or a whole year: switch with Week, Month and Year, and move with the arrows or "This week".
It shows the days you showed up (tap a day to read that evening's report, with your journal if you use it), the six areas compared with the period before, the habits you kept most often, your fullest week and the lines you wrote. A week also has a free note for you.
It only describes, it never grades: a day left blank is empty, not zero, and the comparison is just a difference in numbers. In the first days of a new month, Home shows a card that opens the month that just ended.
guide.review.title: Looking back: week, month and year
guide.score.body:
For each area the score is the share of your habits you kept, counting each habit by its weight. The overall score of a day is the average of the areas that had habits.
A day with nothing filled in is empty, not 0%. Scores are relative to how many habits you had that day, so adding or archiving habits never rewrites the past: each report keeps the habits and weights as they were.
guide.score.title: How the score works
